sections.title: Objective type questions of two 1-mark parts.

questions.q: (a) Find the maximum value of f(x) = 1/(4x² + 2x + 1). (b) Using differentials, find √49.5.
questions.answer:
(a) 4x² + 2x + 1 = 4(x + ¼)² + ¾ has least value ¾ at x = −¼, so f has maximum 4/3.
(b) f(x) = √x, x = 49, Δx = 0.5: √49.5 ≈ 7 + 0.5/(2·7) = 7 + 0.0357 ≈ 7.036.

sections.title: Objective type question of six 1-mark parts.

questions.q: Cost C = x³/3 − 18x² + 160x for x units. Find (i) AC, (ii) MC, (iii) the output where AC = MC, (iv) the output where MC is minimum, (v) the output where AC is minimum, (vi) the minimum MC.
f(x) = (1 − x + x²)/(1 + x + x²). (i) How many critical points? (ii) Their signs? (iii) Nature at the positive one? (iv) Nature at the negative one? (v) Local minimum value? (vi) Local maximum value?
questions.answer:
f'(x) = [(−1 + 2x)(1 + x + x²) − (1 − x + x²)(1 + 2x)]/(1 + x + x²)² = 2(x² − 1)/(1 + x + x²)².
(i) f' = 0 at x = ±1: 2 critical points.
(ii) One positive (1), one negative (−1).
(iii) f' changes − to + at x = 1: local minimum.
(iv) f' changes + to − at x = −1: local maximum.
(v) f(1) = 1/3. (vi) f(−1) = 3/1 = 3.

Find the intervals in which f(x) = 2x³ + x² − 20x is decreasing.
questions.answer:
f'(x) = 6x² + 2x − 20 = 2(3x² + x − 10) = 2(3x − 5)(x + 2).
f' < 0 between the roots: −2 < x < 5/3. Decreasing on (−2, 5/3).

or.answer: If f is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b) and f(a) = f(b), then there is at least one c in (a, b) with f'(c) = 0.

questions.q: Find the intervals in which f(x) = 2x³ − 3x² − 12x + 6 is increasing or decreasing.
questions.answer:
f'(x) = 6x² − 6x − 12 = 6(x − 2)(x + 1).
f' > 0 for x < −1 and x > 2; f' < 0 for −1 < x < 2.
Increasing on (−∞, −1) ∪ (2, ∞); decreasing on (−1, 2).

or.q: Show that the tangents to 6y = 3x⁵ + 2x³ − 3x at x = ±3 are parallel.
or.answer:
6y' = 15x⁴ + 6x² − 3 ⇒ y' = (15x⁴ + 6x² − 3)/6.
Only even powers appear, so y'(3) = y'(−3) = (1215 + 54 − 3)/6 = 211.
Equal slopes ⇒ the tangents are parallel.

questions.q: Find the points where the tangents to y = 2x³ − 15x² + 36x − 21 are parallel to the x-axis, and their equations.
Divide 75 into two parts such that the product of one part and the square of the other is maximum.
questions.answer:
Let the parts be x and 75 − x; P = x²(75 − x) = 75x² − x³.
P' = 150x − 3x² = 3x(50 − x) = 0 ⇒ x = 50. P'' = 150 − 6x = −150 < 0 ⇒ maximum.
Parts: 50 and 25.

questions.q: Verify Lagrange's mean value theorem for f(x) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3) on [0, 4].
questions.answer:
f is a polynomial, so it is continuous on [0, 4] and differentiable on (0, 4).
f(0) = −6, f(4) = 6 ⇒ [f(4) − f(0)]/(4 − 0) = 12/4 = 3.
f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 ⇒ f'(x) = 3x² − 12x + 11.
3c² − 12c + 11 = 3 ⇒ 3c² − 12c + 8 = 0 ⇒ c = 2 ± 2/√3 ≈ 3.15 or 0.85, both in (0, 4).
Hence the theorem is verified.

or.q: Verify Rolle's theorem for f(x) = x(x − 1)(x − 2) on [0, 2].
or.answer:
Polynomial ⇒ continuous and differentiable. f(0) = f(2) = 0.
f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 2x ⇒ f'(x) = 3x² − 6x + 2 = 0 ⇒ c = 1 ± 1/√3 ≈ 1.58 or 0.42, both in (0, 2).
Verified.

questions.q: Show that of all rectangles with a given perimeter, the square has the greatest area.
questions.answer:
Let the perimeter be 2p and the sides x and p − x. Area A = x(p − x) = px − x².
A' = p − 2x = 0 ⇒ x = p/2. A'' = −2 < 0 ⇒ maximum.
Then both sides are p/2: the rectangle is a square.

or.q: Find the point on y² = 4x nearest to (2, 1).
or.answer:
Take the point (t², 2t). D² = (t² − 2)² + (2t − 1)².
d(D²)/dt = 4t(t² − 2) + 4(2t − 1) = 4t³ − 4 = 0 ⇒ t = 1 (second derivative 12t² > 0 ⇒ minimum).
Nearest point: (1, 2).
